doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Quiz on Sidran lyrics: Boom Boom Shaboogie
summary: Monk quotes lyrics; Sidran does not recall them until Boom Boom Shaboogie, and they discuss the shuffle and its structure.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let’s talk about your music for a moment. We’re going to play “continue this Bed Sidran lyric,” okay? I’m going to read something and you see if you remember it. “They’ve been doing it in Brooklyn/Like it’s going out of style/And all the cats in Cleveland/Got a great big smile.”
That’s a relatively recent song. It’s — gosh, boy in the last 15 years I’ve written so many songs.
I’ll give you a hint, it’s something about St. Louis. “Don’t Even Ask About St. Louis.”
You got me. What is it?
I didn’t mean to get you.
“Ahead by a mile/They’ve got that boom-boom-boom shaboogie.”
Oh it’s “Boom Boom Shaboogie” of course. Of course. Well there’s a classic example of something coming out of just a riff. Right. Well that was just being funny.
Yeah and you know of all the musical styles there are, I love a good shuffle.
Yeah. Well it’s the heartbeat man.

There you go. But there’s something that caught me about that song because it starts out with this instrumental groove with a boogie, and the first singing that shows up sounds like it’s on the bridge.
Uh huh. It starts on the four chord. Yeah that’s an old trick. That’s a good old trick. It’s you throw ‘em a curve. So, yeah.
Thank you, thank you. Boy that’s funny. I recognized the intent of the lyric I just couldn’t place it. That’s pretty obscure, Monk, I’m sorry but —
